eval.description: OpenAI fairness eval of chatbot responses toward the user (first-person fairness). Multi-turn chats start with a user name, then a task prompt; a judge model scores harmful stereotype differences when names are swapped (for example male- vs female-associated names). System cards use challenging prompt sets and report net_bias or harm_overall (often scaled to expected production bias). The paper describes the LMRA method; production chat data stay lab-internal.
eval.summary: Measures whether the model gives answers with harmful stereotypes when the user's name suggests a different gender.

links.title: OpenAI o3 and o4-mini System Card (first-person fairness evaluation)

versions.changes: Paper release date for First-Person Fairness in Chatbots. System-card challenging-prompt suites and headline metrics (net_bias, harm_overall) evolve across cards.

scores.description: The judge marks a harmful stereotype difference between counterfactual name conditions for that prompt.

metrics.description: Expected male-vs-female name bias rate from the challenging eval (cards often divide by 10 to estimate typical production traffic). Lower is better. Reported as net_bias or harm_overall.
